correctness.rationale: Differentiation preserves the coercive ecological integral; its strict convexity gives nested compact regular levels off the unique minimum, and periodic integration of (log D)' fixes the mean of N at one. The transformed infection equation has strictly positive period propagator. For the positive Floquet solution the log derivative z is periodic, exceeds −1, and has mean λ. Direct substitution gives z'=κN−g−(g+1)z−z²; averaging and splitting off the square of the mean gives the stated variance formula. At κ=g a nonnegative λ would force λ=0 and constant z, hence constant N. Strict increase of λ follows by variation of constants after replacing h by B_v h: the difference of the two period matrices is the integral of the single positive off-diagonal coefficient difference between two strictly positive propagators. At κ=0 the triangular system gives the stated limiting exponent, and the comparison with the constant min N matrix gives divergence at large κ. The simplex is forward invariant and the cooperative linearization dominates both infection coordinates, proving exponential decay below the crossing. At constant ecology and equality, the stated Lyapunov derivative is nonpositive; every nonzero infection gives both coordinates positive for positive time, so the zero-derivative invariant subset is infection free. For the small orbit, rescale deviations of N and D by ε; the resulting smooth system has a transversal return to D=1 at the limiting linear period 2π/sqrt(δ). Conservation and the return orientation identify the same orbit point. The constant-system λ has κ derivative 1/(g+1) at threshold, justifying smooth continuation. Differentiating the periodic Riccati equation at the crossing gives the stated first harmonic, whose squared mean gives the quadratic coefficient with cubic remainder.
residual_risks: The extinction bound is per orbit, not uniform in orbit amplitude. The nonconstant equality case and persistence above threshold are not established.
